questions.question: The decision-making body of a village panchayat, consisting of all adult voters of the village who meet at least twice or thrice a year, is called the:
options: Gram Sabha
Nyaya Panchayat
Zilla Parishad
Block Samiti
questions.explanation: The Gram Panchayat works under the overall supervision of the Gram Sabha. All the voters in the village are its members. It has to meet at least twice or thrice in a year to approve the annual budget and review performance.

questions.question: A few Gram Panchayats are grouped together to form what is usually called a:
options: Panchayat Samiti, Block, or Mandal
Zilla Parishad
Gram Sabha
Municipal Corporation
questions.explanation: A few Gram Panchayats are grouped together to form what is usually called a Panchayat Samiti or Block or Mandal. The members of this representative body are elected by all the panchayat members in that area.

questions.question: All the Panchayat Samitis or Mandals in a district together constitute the Zilla (district) Parishad. Who is the political head of the Zilla Parishad?
options: Zilla Parishad Chairperson
District Magistrate (Collector)
State Governor
Mayor
questions.explanation: Zilla Parishad Chairperson is the political head of the Zilla Parishad. Members of the Lok Sabha and MLAs of that district and some other officials of other district-level bodies are also its members.

questions.question: Big cities are constituted into Municipal Corporations. What is the elected political head of a Municipal Corporation called?
options: Mayor
Municipal Commissioner
Sarpanch
Governor
questions.explanation: Municipalities are set up in towns. Big cities are constituted into Municipal Corporations. Both are controlled by elected bodies. Municipal Chairperson is the political head of the municipality. In a Municipal Corporation such an officer is called the Mayor.

questions.question: How did Indian leaders handle the language dispute in 1965 when English was scheduled to cease as an official language?
options: The Central Government agreed to continue the use of English along with Hindi for official purposes, showing flexibility
The Central Government forcefully banned English across all universities
All non-Hindi states were expelled from the Indian Union
Hindi was made compulsory for all private businesses
questions.explanation: According to the Constitution, the use of English for official purposes was to stop in 1965. However, many non-Hindi speaking States demanded that the use of English continue. The Central Government responded by agreeing to continue the use of English along with Hindi for official purposes. Promotion of Hindi continues to be official policy, but promotion does not mean imposition.

questions.question: States such as Assam, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh, and Mizoram enjoy special constitutional provisions under Article 371 primarily due to:
options: Protection of land rights of indigenous indigenous peoples, customary laws, and preferential employment
Total exemption from paying income tax or customs duties
Right to print their own state currency notes
Right to sign military treaties with neighbouring foreign countries
questions.explanation: Some States enjoy a special status under Article 371 due to their peculiar social and historical circumstances. These special powers are especially enjoyable with respect to protection of land rights of indigenous peoples, their culture and also preferential employment in government services.

questions.question: Why does a federal constitution explicitly specify the sources of revenue for each level of government?
options: To ensure its financial autonomy and operational independence
To allow the central government to confiscate all state bank accounts
To ensure that citizens pay zero taxes to municipal councils
To prevent states from spending money on public schools
questions.explanation: Sources of revenue for each level of government are clearly specified to ensure its financial autonomy. A government cannot remain truly federal without independent financial resources.

questions.question: Prior to 1990, the Central Government often dismissed State Governments led by rival political parties under Article 356 (President's Rule). What major development curtailed this undemocratic practice?
options: A landmark Supreme Court judgment making arbitrary dismissal difficult, along with the rise of regional coalition governance
Total abolition of the office of State Governor
A complete ban on political party formation in states
The United Nations Security Council intervention
questions.explanation: A major judgment of the Supreme Court made it difficult for the Central Government to dismiss state governments in an arbitrary manner. Coupled with the era of coalition governments, this significantly strengthened federal autonomy post-1990.

questions.question: What are the two core dual objectives of a federal system?
options: To safeguard and promote unity of the country, while at the same time accommodating regional diversity
To eliminate regional cultural identities and enforce total uniformity
To maximize central military expenditure and reduce social welfare
To replace democratic elections with judicial decrees
questions.explanation: Federal system has dual objectives: to safeguard and promote unity of the country, while at the same time accommodate regional diversity.

questions.question: India's constitutional experiment in local self-governance is the largest experiment in democracy anywhere in the world. Approximately how many elected representatives are there in rural and urban local bodies?
options: About 36 lakh (3.6 million) elected representatives
About 50,000 representatives
About 1 lakh representatives
About 10 million representatives
questions.explanation: There are now about 36 lakh elected representatives in the panchayats and municipalities etc., all over the country. This number is bigger than the population of many countries in the world.

questions.question: States like Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat were reorganized or created primarily on the basis of:
options: Linguistic identity (language spoken by people)
Religious majorities
Height of mountain ranges
Annual rainfall levels
questions.explanation: In 1947, the boundaries of several old States of India were changed in order to create new States. This was done to ensure that people who spoke the same language lived in the same State.

questions.subtopic: States Created on Culture and Ethnicity
questions.question: Which group of Indian states was created not on the basis of language, but to recognize differences based on culture, ethnicity, or geography?
options: Nagaland, Uttarakhand, and Jharkhand
Punjab and Haryana
Kerala and Tamil Nadu
Odisha and West Bengal
questions.explanation: Some States were created not on the basis of language but to recognise differences based on culture, ethnicity or geography. These include States like Nagaland, Uttarakhand and Jharkhand.

questions.question: While constitutional status for local government has deepened democracy in India, what remains a significant continuing challenge?
options: Many state governments have not transferred significant powers and adequate revenue resources to local bodies
Villagers refuse to vote in panchayat elections
The Supreme Court declared Panchayati Raj unconstitutional
Panchayats are prohibited from maintaining village roads
questions.explanation: While elections are held regularly, Gram Sabhas are not held regularly. Most state governments have not transferred significant powers to the local governments, nor have they given adequate resources.

questions.question: The city of Porto Alegre in Brazil is globally renowned in democratic theory for developing which innovative local governance mechanism?
options: Participatory Democracy where local citizens directly deliberate on the city budget
A complete military dictatorship with zero municipal taxation
A city ruled entirely by artificial intelligence computer algorithms
Privatisation of all municipal roads and parks
questions.explanation: The city of Porto Alegre set up a parallel organisation operating alongside the municipal council, where nearly 50,000 citizens participate in meetings to decide how the municipal budget should be spent.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Civics, Chapter 2, Section 4 (Box Story: Porto Alegre)

questions.question: Both the Central Government and State Governments can enact environmental and wildlife conservation regulations because 'Forests' are placed in the:
options: Concurrent List
Union List
State List
Residuary List
questions.explanation: Forests, education, trade unions, marriage, adoption, and succession are placed in the Concurrent List, allowing both Centre and States to make laws.

questions.question: The legal authority of a government or court over a specific territory, subject matter, or category of citizens is formally defined as:
options: Jurisdiction
Sovereign immunity
Diplomatic protocol
Veto prerogative
questions.explanation: Jurisdiction is the area over which someone has legal authority. The area may be defined in terms of geographical boundaries or in terms of certain kinds of subjects.

questions.question: In 'Holding Together' federations like India, constituent states:
options: Very often do not have equal powers; some units are granted special powers or asymmetrical status
Always possess identical identical constitutional authority and independent militaries
Can secede unilaterally from the union at any moment
Have zero control over their state police departments
questions.explanation: In 'holding together' federations, the central government tends to be more powerful vis-a-vis the States. Very often different constituent units of the federation have unequal powers; some units are granted special powers.

questions.question: Each village or a group of villages in some states has a Gram Panchayat. The directly elected president or head of the panchayat is called the:
options: Sarpanch
Mayor
Collector
Governor
questions.explanation: Each village or a group of villages has a Gram Panchayat. This is a council consisting of several ward members, often called panch, and a president or Sarpanch.

questions.question: According to the Indian Constitution, the official policy of promoting Hindi as an official language:
options: Does not mean that the Central Government can impose Hindi on States where people speak a different language
Mandates that all citizens must pass a compulsory Hindi speaking exam
Allows the Centre to dismiss any non-Hindi speaking Chief Minister
Prohibits state civil services from using regional languages
questions.explanation: Promotion of Hindi continues to be the official policy of the Government of India. But promotion does not mean that the Central Government can impose Hindi on States where people speak a different language.

questions.question: The success of Indian federalism depends not merely on constitutional provisions, but fundamentally on:
options: The nature of democratic politics, respect for diversity, and shared desire for living together
The size of the national standing army
The price of crude oil in international markets
The total number of national holidays declared each year
questions.explanation: Constitutional provisions are necessary for the success of federalism but these are not sufficient. The real success of federalism in India can be attributed to the nature of democratic politics in our country.
